feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Author Tomi Adeyemi contends with reality in her new book, 'The Siren'
entry.summary: The author Tomi Adeyemi has written fantasy all her life. Now, she has a new book out titled The Siren, which takes place in the real world.

entry.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
entry.summary: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating now them.

entry.title: The WHO seeks more details on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia
entry.summary: The World Health Organization says it wants more information on what caused the death of an employee at a Russian plague research lab. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

entry.title: New novel — 'Friends and Family' — offers raw and frank look at race and class
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with Natalize Baszile about her new novel Friends and Family. Can an interracial friendship stand up to the pressure of U.S. life in 2026?

entry.title: Judge orders Tennessee to preserve evidence in failed execution
entry.summary: Lawyers for Christa Pike, the woman who survived an execution in Tennessee, were in court Wednesday as she regained consciousness.

entry.title: At 100, Juneteenth's 'grandmother' Opal Lee vows to 'keep on walking' for social issues
entry.summary: Opal Lee, considered the grandmother of Juneteenth, turned 100 years old. She attended a ceremony at the site of the planned Juneteenth Museum in Fort Worth featuring former first lady Michelle Obama.

entry.title: FBI counterintelligence squads are now severely understaffed, as threats only grow
entry.summary: NPR's exclusive reporting shows that the FBI teams that hunt foreign spies are severely understaffed, down as much as 50 percent in some offices.

entry.title: Reflecting on soccer superstar Lionel Messi's unrivaled career
entry.summary: Lionel Messi played his last game for Argentina's national team on Tuesday. NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer reflects on his career and legacy with CBS Sports commentator Nico Cantor.

entry.title: BTS frontman RM is showing his art collection. Fans are flocking to see it
entry.summary: A K-pop idol and leader of BTS turns museum curator with a new exhibition at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art.

entry.title: New global survey shows danger of heat for pregnant people and newborns
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with epidemiologist Rupa Basu about a new survey of 1,000 health professionals, which found that extreme heat is posing a growing threat to pregnant people and newborns.
